Question: Does the platform support sample-based auditing with configurable confidence intervals, stratified by risk level?
Response: Yes. Statistical QC is implemented through the Fleet Manager agent and Foundry Evaluators. The Fleet Manager can configure sample-based auditing: (1) Random sampling — 10% of completed workflows are flagged for human review. (2) Stratified by risk — high-risk workflows (high-value invoices, senior hires) have higher sampling rates. (3) Configurable confidence intervals — the sampling rate adjusts based on desired statistical confidence. The Fleet Manager composes the QC queue on the Control Plane: selected workflows are presented to the operator with full context for review. QC results (human confirms agent decision, or human overrides) feed back into quality metrics and threshold calibration. This is not a pre-built statistical QC product — it is implemented through Fleet Manager skills that encode the sampling logic and Foundry Evaluators that score quality.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent (sampling logic), Foundry Evaluators (quality scoring), Control Plane (QC queue)
POC Demo: POC2: Show statistical QC — 10% sample of screening decisions flagged for HR BP review, stratified by candidate seniority.

Question: Can independent evaluator agents audit worker agents using separate criteria, models, and data; provably independent (no shared memory)?
Response: Yes — at two levels. (1) Inside each phase the MAF workflow graph expresses James's "judge catches executioner" pattern structurally: a validator executor node sits downstream of an agent executor node with an explicit edge between them. The validator does not share the agent's LLM context — it runs deterministic rule engines or, when reasoning is required, invokes a separate GHCP SDK session with a different system prompt and different (often cheaper and different-provider) model. Judge/executioner separation is a graph topology, not a prompt trick. (2) Across the fleet, the Fleet Manager agent is a separate domain-scoped Hosted Agent (fleet-manager@wpp) with its own Entra identity, its own model configuration and read-only access to telemetry — it does not share memory or execution context with the domain agents it monitors. Foundry Evaluators run as separate evaluation pipelines with their own model configurations. Independence is provable: separate Entra identity, separate Hosted Agent container, separate model deployment, read-only access, explicit MAF graph edges. For maximum independence the auditing evaluator (or validator agent executor) uses a different model provider than the audited agent.
Key Technologies: Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) validator executors (judge/executioner graph separation), Fleet Manager (independent auditor), separate Entra identity, separate model deployment, Foundry Evaluators (independent pipeline)
POC Demo: POC2: Show Fleet Manager auditing screening decisions using a different model — independent evaluation with separate criteria, provably no shared memory.

Question: Describe continuous behavioural monitoring against baselines with alerts for unusual tool usage, escalation changes, quality shifts, cost spikes.
Response: Continuous behavioural monitoring operates at four layers. (1) APIM AI Gateway: per-agent, per-tool usage patterns with statistical baselines; anomalies on tool call frequency, access patterns, token usage trigger alerts. (2) MAF validator executors: per-workflow pass/fail signals on agent executor outputs — rising validator failure rate is an early drift indicator. (3) Foundry Evaluators: continuous evaluation on production traffic against quality baselines; Task Adherence detects behavioural drift from defined purpose. (4) Fleet Manager: reasons about fleet-wide patterns across all signals. Detects unusual escalation rate changes, cost spikes, quality shifts, tool usage pattern changes. Alerts surface on the Control Plane with context and recommended action. Alerting integrates with Azure Monitor and Microsoft Sentinel.
Key Technologies: APIM anomaly detection, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) validator executors (drift signal), Foundry Evaluators (behavioural baseline), Fleet Manager (fleet-wide patterns), Azure Monitor, Microsoft Sentinel
POC Demo: POC1: Simulate cost spike — show anomaly detection triggering Fleet Manager alert on Control Plane with root cause analysis.

Question: Can outputs be clearly marked as agent-generated, human-generated, or human-reviewed; configurable per client and regulatory context?
Response: Yes. All outputs carry provenance metadata. (1) Agent-generated: outputs produced by a MAF agent executor (GHCP SDK session) are marked with agent identity, skill version, model used, MAF workflow + executor ID. OTEL spans — MAF workflow spans plus GHCP SDK session spans — provide full provenance chain. (2) Human-reviewed: outputs that passed HITL approval carry approver identity and timestamp; the action ledger distinguishes autonomous from human-approved actions. (3) Human-generated: direct human actions are attributed to the human's identity. Configurable per context: skills add explicit transparency markings (e.g. "AI-generated shortlist, reviewed by [HR BP]"). EU AI Act: the compliance skill adds required disclosures. Per-client transparency configurable in workflow metadata.
Key Technologies: OTEL provenance metadata (MAF + GHCP SDK), Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) executor/workflow IDs, action ledger (audit attribution), skill-configurable transparency markings, Entra identity attribution
POC Demo: POC2: Show transparency marking on screening output — 'AI-generated shortlist, reviewed by [HR BP]' with full provenance chain.

Question: If a primary model provider goes down, can agents fail over to alternative models with acceptable quality? Describe the model-abstraction layer and cross-model eval baselines.
Response: Yes. APIM AI Gateway provides the model-abstraction layer with built-in failover. Configuration: (1) Primary model endpoint (e.g. Azure OpenAI GPT-4.1). (2) Fallback model endpoint. (3) APIM health checks detect unavailability and route to fallback without agent restart. GHCP SDK is model-agnostic — an agent executor works with any model from the Foundry catalog; skills specify acceptable alternatives. MAF agent executors inherit this — model abstraction happens below the graph node. Cross-model eval baselines: Foundry Evaluators run quality assessments on both primary and fallback models; fallback is pre-validated for minimum quality per skill. If fallback quality is below acceptable, Fleet Manager surfaces a degradation alert and can increase HITL oversight (raise MAF validator strictness, raise autonomy thresholds) until primary recovers.
Key Technologies: APIM AI Gateway (model failover), Foundry model catalog, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) agent executors (model-agnostic), Foundry Evaluators (cross-model baseline), Fleet Manager (degradation alerts)
POC Demo: POC1: Simulate primary model endpoint failure — show APIM failover to alternative model, Fleet Manager notification of degraded mode, quality comparison on Control Plane.

Question: Describe platform-level circuit breakers preventing cascading failures. What is brown-out mode (partial work, queue for humans)? How does automatic failover to human queues work?
Response: Circuit breakers operate at multiple levels. (1) APIM AI Gateway: circuit breaker policies detect repeated failures on model endpoints or MCP tool calls. After configurable threshold APIM opens the circuit; retries periodically to detect recovery. (2) MAF workflow: failing executors can raise typed errors that route via conditional edges to brown-out branches (cached-data executor, HITL gate executor) rather than retrying indefinitely. (3) Durable Functions: retry policies with max attempts prevent a single failing phase from blocking the workflow indefinitely; after max retries, phase enters exception state. (4) Fleet Manager: detects cascading patterns (e.g. Workday API down affecting all finance workflows) and alerts proactively. Brown-out mode: when a dependency degrades, agent executors proceed with cached data or partial results; Fleet Manager switches affected workflows to increased-HITL mode via autonomy config updates. Automatic failover to human queues: when circuit breakers trip, pending work is composed with full context and routed to the operator's PA. Control Plane shows which workflows are in brown-out mode.
Key Technologies: APIM circuit breakers, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) conditional-edge brown-out routing, Azure Durable Functions retry limits, Fleet Manager (cascading failure detection), brown-out mode (increased HITL)
POC Demo: POC1: Simulate Workday API degradation — show circuit breaker tripping, brown-out mode activation, affected workflows routed to Finance BP queue.
